guidance.top_category: Use one broad family only. Do not create new category names. Choose by the clause's main legal effect, not by isolated keywords.
guidance.suggested_cluster_name: Free-form snake_case subtype in your own words, e.g. unilateral_price_increase_due_to_inflation.
guidance.source_span: Exact contiguous text copied from item text. No ellipses or paraphrase.
guidance.risk_or_safe: Classify the legal effect from the affected party's perspective, especially the consumer/client/weaker party. Do not equate every obligation with risk and do not mark ordinary statutory/default wording risky unless it creates a concrete disadvantage, removes a protection, or appears in a consumer-unfavorable contract clause.
risk_precedence: For statutes, judgments, and official forms, use neutral for ordinary default rules, definitions, balanced procedural mechanics, and background legal allocations unless the span itself clearly creates a protective right or an unfair burden.

For consumer contract/UOKiK clauses, use risky when the clause limits/excludes liability, weakens remedies, delays refund/performance, imposes penalties/fees, creates unilateral discretion, restricts access/use/termination/withdrawal, shifts burdens to the consumer, or creates procedural traps or forum disadvantages.

Use safe when the clause grants or preserves a protective right, remedy, refund, warranty, complaint path, withdrawal/termination right, transparency duty, or trader/provider duty that benefits the consumer/client/weaker party.
Use neutral for definitions, ordinary statutory defaults, balanced administrative mechanics, factual background, or clauses where no clear advantage/disadvantage is created by the span itself.
Use unknown only when the span is too fragmentary to classify even after considering context.
If both protective and risky effects appear, classify by the dominant operative effect in the selected source_span and explain the tradeoff in risk_reason.
guidance.service_quality_scope: Use service_quality only when the main legal effect is a quality or proper-performance standard: defects, warranty/rękojmia/gwarancja, conformity with contract, agreed service standard, or repair/replacement of defective performance.
service_quality_precedence: If the main legal effect is a contractual fine, penalty, or interest for poor service, use penalty_or_interest.
If the main legal effect is a missed deadline, extended repair time, delayed delivery, or delayed performance, use delivery_or_performance_delay.
If the main legal effect is limiting, excluding, or allocating responsibility for bad quality, use liability.
If the main legal effect is a complaint, notice, reporting, or claim procedure/deadline, use complaint_or_notice.
If the main legal effect is a unilateral right to change, restrict, suspend, block, or degrade a service, use unilateral_change or property_or_use_restriction.
If the main legal effect is a monetary refund, fee reduction, discount, or price consequence, use payment.
Use service_quality only when none of those more specific effects dominates.
